title: The City Beyond
notes: A level (D-59): a scenario on a map. map: which data/maps file; start: the stranger's first cell; objective: the long goal shown when no step is running; goal: how the HUD's tracker puts it when there's no lead to follow; cast: who is here, each person's routine (role: the short title over them; step_ms: their pace; goal; anchors: [x, y, activity on arrival, dwell ms], the first is where they start; keeps_gate: a gate guard, who won't leave the gate short of guards; conditions: what ails them at the start, as {kind, area}, e.g. Kade's aching knees); things: what lies about or is carried at the start, each a thing as in content/world_objects.json, or the name of a content file whose objects are all included. A level with steps is a guided story (scenario.py; see the training levels). base: another level whose map, start, objective and cast this one takes, and whose things it adds to. A training level also has track (basic, advanced, or test for the developer's own), order, minutes (how long it should take), teaches (short phrases) and blurb (one line), shown on the Training screen; hidden keeps it to developer builds. The village is the main game: no steps, no track. stories: the storylines that run here (content/stories.json, D-61). Each step's playtest is what a scripted playtest does there (tools/playtest_level.gd, and the words eval, evals/run_level_words.py): walk_to (a person, a thing or [x, y]), take, say (to), do (to), ui, ask. try_also: other words for a do step, which the words eval tries too.
goal: Find a way into the city
